Represent a research job as a durable state machine containing the user objective, constraints, plan, evidence records, remaining time/token budget, and pending tool calls. Ask a clarifying question when an unresolved choice would change the research scope or produce an unusable result; do not ask for facts retrievable from permitted sources.

A planner decomposes the objective into evidence-seeking questions. Execute independent searches concurrently under bounded fan-out, deduplicate URLs, and retain source dates, excerpts, and citation IDs. The controller decides whether another search can close a specific evidence gap; cap depth, tool count, retries, and spend. Retrieved pages are untrusted evidence, not instructions to the agent. Tool credentials and side-effect permissions remain outside model control.

Compact context into claims, supporting evidence IDs, contradictions, and unfinished questions rather than discarding provenance. For an illustrative 60-second interactive budget, reserve time for synthesis and allow only bounded research waves; offer a resumable background job for larger requests. Evaluate factual support, coverage, contradiction handling, completion rate, and cost per successful task. A timeout should return a clearly partial report with preserved evidence, not a fabricated conclusion.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** Treat each tool step as a state transition $s_{t+1}=F(s_t,a_t,o_t)$ recorded durably. Retry read operations safely and attach idempotency keys or approval gates to externally consequential writes. Evaluate final evidence quality and task completion under a fixed budget, since more tool calls can increase cost and error exposure without improving the result.
